test_title: PYST 1: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 27 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is NOT used for expressing the concentration of a solution?

options.text: Volume by Volume percentage of a solution
Mass by volume percentage of a solution
Volume by Mass percentage of a solution
Mass by mass percentage of a solution

solution:
The correct answer is __**Volume by Mass percentage of a solution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Volume by Volume percentage (v/v%)**: This is a common way to express the concentration of a solution, particularly for liquids. It is calculated as the volume of the solute divided by the total volume of the solution, multiplied by 100. **Example:** Alcohol in water solutions.
 
• **Mass by Volume percentage (m/v%)**: This is a widely used method in laboratories and industries. It represents the mass of the solute in grams per 100 mL of the solution. **Example:** Saline solution (NaCl in water).
 
• **Volume by Mass percentage (v/m%)**: This method is **not commonly used** for expressing the concentration of a solution, as it does not align with standard practices in chemistry. This inconsistency in units makes it impractical and rarely adopted.
 
• **Mass by Mass percentage (m/m%)**: This is another standard way to express concentration. It is the mass of the solute divided by the total mass of the solution, multiplied by 100. **Example:** Sugar in water solutions.
 
• The correct answer is **Volume by Mass percentage**, as it is not a standard method for expressing the concentration of a solution in scientific or industrial contexts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Concentration of a solution:** It refers to the amount of solute that is dissolved in a given quantity of solvent. It is usually expressed as a percentage or in molarity, molality, or normality.
 
• **Molarity (M):** It is the number of moles of solute per liter of solution. It is one of the most commonly used units of concentration in chemistry. **Example:** 1 M NaOH solution contains 1 mole of NaOH per liter of solution.
 
• **Molality (m):** It is the number of moles of solute per kilogram of solvent. Unlike molarity, it is not affected by temperature changes as it depends on mass rather than volume.
 
• **Normality (N):** It is the number of gram-equivalents of solute per liter of solution. It is often used in acid-base reactions and redox reactions.
 
• **Parts per Million (ppm):** It is a unit of concentration used for very dilute solutions, representing the number of parts of solute per million parts of solution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Applications of concentration expressions:**

 
 
• **Volume by Volume percentage:** Commonly used in industries like alcoholic beverages and cosmetics.
 
• **Mass by Volume percentage:** Frequently utilized in pharmaceutical preparations and clinical solutions like glucose solutions or saline.
 
• **Mass by Mass percentage:** Used in food and chemical industries for solid mixtures.
 
 
 
• **Importance of standardization:** The use of standardized units like molarity, molality, and percentage ensures uniformity in scientific communication and industrial processes.
 
• **Practicality in laboratory settings:** Units like molarity and mass by volume percentage are preferred due to ease of measurement and preparation of solutions.
